headline: Neighbors already recommend you. Google hasn't met you yet.
summary: HighTop Construction is a solo contractor in El Cajon, the kind of local shop neighbors pass along when they need a project done. On Nextdoor you were named a Neighborhood Favorite in 2025, and a June 2025 review says you were responsive, professional, and made a difficult process seamless. You replied to that neighbor a few days later. The biggest leftover is Google. We couldn't find a Google listing for HighTop Construction at all, so anyone who hears your name and searches for it in El Cajon comes up empty. A free Google Business Profile, set up as a service-area business so a home address stays private, would give that reputation a clear place to land. One smaller thing to settle first: your Nextdoor page title uses HighTop, and at least one review writes it Hi Top. Picking one spelling before the listing goes up will keep the name consistent.

signals.note: When we searched Google's business listings for HighTop Construction in El Cajon, nothing came back for you. Similar names popped up, but they were different businesses. Your Nextdoor page is clearly working, including a Neighborhood Favorite nod in 2025. Customers who aren't on Nextdoor have no way to find you.
signals.next: Set up a free Google Business Profile as a service-area business, so a home address stays private, and list El Cajon and the nearby areas you cover. Use the name you want to be known by, and pick categories that match the work you actually take on.

signals.note: Your number, (619) 314-2466, is on your Nextdoor page, and that's a solid place for neighbors to reach you. A referred customer can call you on the first try.
signals.next: Keep (619) 314-2466 as the single number everywhere, including a new Google listing.

signals.note: We didn't get a clear hours listing from our first look at your Nextdoor page. If hours aren't posted, people may not know when it's a good time to call.
signals.next: Add the hours you usually take calls to your Nextdoor page, and use the same hours on Google once the listing is up.

signals.note: Without a Google listing, there's no place for searchers to see examples of your work. For construction jobs, a few clear photos do a lot of the convincing.
signals.next: On your next few jobs, with the homeowner's okay, snap a couple of photos and add them to the Google listing once it exists.

signals.note: We didn't find a website for HighTop Construction. For a one-person construction business that's normal, but it means Nextdoor is your only home online. A Google listing can cover most of what a small website would.
signals.next: Start with the Google listing and use your Nextdoor page as its website link, so searchers can see what neighbors say. A simple one-page site can wait until you want it.

signals.note: Your phone and El Cajon location are consistent on Nextdoor. The name itself isn't quite settled: the page title says HighTop, and at least one review says Hi Top. Your Nextdoor page also shows a street that looks residential, so we'd leave that off a public listing.
signals.next: Pick one spelling of the name and use it everywhere, including Google. Set the Google listing up as a service-area business so a home address stays private, and keep the same name, number, and service area in both places.
